request.spec:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the
cut as shown (empty when none).
request.prompt:

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export pools (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-pools"`) next to the existing people and claims export buttons. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

It's a front-end change only, in `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`. When pressed, the button re-reads the sheet's pools from the server and downloads `pools-<sheet>.csv`. The file has the header `pool,member,share,cut`, then one line per member:
- Pools and their members come in the order they were added.
- A member pool is written as `pool:<name>`.
- The cut is the same value the pool's line shows, or empty when there isn't one.
- Values containing a comma are quoted, using the same rule as the other exports (e.g. `"Lee, Jo"`).

No server changes, stored data or audit records were needed, because the pools endpoint already returns the shares and cuts.
